questions.stem: In case of a civil case, if the witness feels that the amount of fees paid to him is less

options.label: A
options.text: He can inform the judge about it

options.label: B
options.text: He can write a letter to the lawyer stating his grievance

options.label: C
options.text: He can’t get any kind of increment in the fees since it’s a civil case

options.label: D
options.text: They get a fixed money of rupees 100 in order to meet the expenses

questions.answerText: He can inform the judge about it
questions.solutionHtml:
He can inform the judge about it
  • CONDUCT MONEY: It is the fee offered or paid to a witness in civil cases, at the time of serving the summons to meet the expenses for attending the Court.
  • If the fee is not paid, or if he feels that the amount is less, the doctor can bring this fact to the notice of the Judge before giving evidence in the Court.
  • The Judge will decide the amount to be paid. In criminal cases, no fee is paid to the witness at the time of serving the summons.
  • He must attend the Court and give evidence because of the interest of the State in securing justice; otherwise, he will be charged with contempt of Court.
  • However, in criminal cases, conveyance charges and daily allowance can be claimed by the doctor according to Government rules.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 9 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 7

questions.stem: According to Supreme Court, every hospital is required to issue a death certificate after the death in the hospital. All are true about the death certificate, except

options.label: A
options.text: Is issued by a registered medical practitioner after thoroughly inspecting the body

options.label: B
options.text: Should be issued only after payment of fees

options.label: C
options.text: Should inform the police before issuing the death certificate if suspicious of foul play

options.label: D
options.text: Issuing or signing a false certificate is punishable under S. 197, I.P.C

questions.answerText: Should be issued only after payment of fees
questions.solutionHtml:
Should be issued only after payment of fees
  • A medical practitioner is legally bound to give a death certificate, stating the cause of death without charging a fee, if a person whom he has been attending during his last illness dies (Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1970)



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 9 ,10 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 8

questions.stem: A stab victim was admitted to the emergency. He was about to die and wanted to talk about the incident. The doctor decided to record the dying declaration. The false statement about the dying declaration is

options.label: A
options.text: A dying declaration is dealt with in Section 32 IPC

options.label: B
options.text: If there is time, the Executive magistrate should be called to record the declaration.

options.label: C
options.text: The statement can also be recorded by the village headman or police

options.label: D
options.text: Leading questions should not be put

questions.answerText: A dying declaration is dealt with in Section 32 IPC
questions.solutionHtml:
A dying declaration is dealt with in Section 32 IPC
  • DYING DECLARATION: It is a written or oral statement of a person, who is dying as a result of some unlawful act, relating to the material facts of the cause of his death or bearing on the circumstances (S.32, I.E.A.).



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 10,11 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 8, 9

questions.stem: Person A’s earlier statement regarding the facts on oath and subsequent statement on oath are opposite to each other, and they cannot be reconciled. Therefore person A can be punished under

options.label: A
options.text: IPC 193

options.label: B
options.text: IPC 191

options.label: C
options.text: IPC 197

options.label: D
options.text: IPC 201

questions.solutionHtml:
IPC 193
  • The witness is liable to be prosecuted for perjury, and the imprisonment may extend to seven years (S. 193, I.P.C.).



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 13 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 10, 40

options.text: It consists of questions put to him by the lawyer (counsel or advocate) for the side which has summoned him.

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.text: The doctor should help the prosecutor in framing proper questions in proper sequence so that all essential facts are elicited.

options.label: D
options.text: ln, a criminal trial, the burden to prove is always on the prosecution (adversarial system of trial).

questions.answerText: In this leading questions are allowed.
questions.solutionHtml:
In this leading questions are allowed.
  • In this leading questions are not allowed, except in those cases, where the Judge is satisfied that a witness is hostile (S.I42 and 154, I.E.A.)

questions.stem: Hair, a knife and a blood-stained handkerchief were collected from a crime scene place. All the specimens were then verified and later produced to the court. Which among the following term describes the method of verification of collected objects from the time until it's produced in the court?

options.label: A
options.text: Chain of custody of specimens

options.label: B
options.text: Chain of custody of evidence

options.label: C
options.text: Chain of collection of specimens

options.label: D
options.text: Chain of collection of evidence

questions.solutionHtml:
Chain of custody of evidence

Chain of Custody of Evidence:

  • It is a method to verify the actual possession of an object from the time it was first identified until it is offered as evidence in Court.
  • Each specimen when obtained should be labelled with the victim's name, the time and date, the nature of the specimen, and identification number, and signed by the doctor.
  • This information must be documented each time the material is handled by another person, and that person must give a receipt for the material and be included in the chain of custody.
  • The evidence must not be damaged. Contaminated, or altered in any significant way. The shorter the chain the better.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 12 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 9

questions.stem: Re-examination of a witness is conducted by:

options.label: A
options.text: Public prosecutor

options.label: B
options.text: Defense lawyer

options.label: C
options.text: Judge

options.label: D
options.text: Police officer

questions.solutionHtml:
Public prosecutor

Re-examination (Re-direct examination):-

  • This is conducted by the lawyer for the side which has called the witness.
  • The object is to correct any mistake or to clarify or add details to the statements the witness has made in cross-examination.
  • It is an opportunity for the witness to explain more fully some answer which might appear damaging to his direct evidence, because of skilful questioning or tactics by the cross-examiner.
  • The witness should not bring in any new matter at this stage.
  • The opposing lawyer has the right of re-cross-examination on the new point raised.
  • Leading questions are not allowed.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 13 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 12

questions.stem: While giving evidence in court the Judge can ask questions at:

options.label: A
options.text: Examination–in–chief

options.label: B
options.text: Cross-examination.

options.label: C
options.text: Re-examination

options.label: D
options.text: Any stage

questions.solutionHtml:
Any stage
  • The Judge may ask any question, in any form, about any fact. Relevant or irrelevant, at any stage of the examination to clear up doubts.
  • The Court is also empowered to recall and re-examine any witness already examined.
  • If his evidence appears to the Court to be essential to the just decision of the Court



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 14 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 12
